newsitem.title: USA: U.S. still recognises Kengo as Zaire premier.
newsitem.headline: U.S. still recognises Kengo as Zaire premier.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it continued to recognise Kengo wa Dondo as prime minister of Zaire, which is gripped by an armed rebellion, despite a vote in Zaire's transitional parliament to oust him.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told a regular news conference it was unclear whether Tuesday's parliamentary vote was constitutionally sound and it was up to the Zairean people to decide that.
"Until they figure it out, it seems to us to be the best way forward to continue to recognise the Kengo government and to work with it," he said.

"I think it's true that Prime Minister Kengo does retain a significant degree of power both over civil agencies and also over military in Zaire, although it is a very complicated, complex scene," he added.

He noted that leaders of other African states in the region had taken a similar decision, indicated by their participation in talks with Kengo in Nairobi on Wednesday at which they issued an appeal for a ceasefire in the Zaire conflict. Burns said Washington joined in that appeal.

He said the State Department had seen reports that President Mobutu Sese Seko was making plans to return to Kinshasa from France, where he has had medical treatment, but the United States did not have a position on that.

"Our position is that we'd like to see a ceasefire, we'd like to see humanitarian assistance for the refugees and we'd like to see the Zairean government and political structurer agree to a reform process that would at some point lead to elections," he said.
Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms in October and vowed to topple Mobutu have made fast progress in eastern Zaire, taking many towns including the regional centre Kisangani.
